items.label: Honeywell Deutsche Bank’s Chicago Industrials Summit 2026 (08-11-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CFO Mike Stepniak on Industrial Automation (now a pure-play

set.signal: CFO Mike Stepniak on Industrial Automation (now a pure-play sensing and measurement business): on time to first promise is about 80%, targeted north of 85%, with on time to Customer One Day the more important metric; growth of 'single digit plus in the second half', and next year 'a really good, I would say, line of sight to grow double from the single digits' on new products and execution; about a 22% margin rate in the fourth quarter and '100% confident' in the 25% three-year margin target. Industrial Automation is close to a $4 billion business that Honeywell would like to be $7 billion, 'much harder to get to $7 billion without doing any M&A'; bolt-on M&A of a $2 billion-$4 billion ticket size is focused mainly on Industrial Automation, must be accretive, in the sensing and measurement core and reach a 10% ROI by year 5; a large transformational deal is 'probably not a priority'.

items.reason: The quoted words 'a really good line of sight' are the CFO's Building Automation wording; for Industrial Automation he said 'a really good, I would say, line of sight to grow double from the single digits' - quote exactly instead of paraphrasing to 'double digits'.
items.evidence: So Pete is going to grow those single digits, those single digit plus in the second half. Next year he has a really good, I would say, line of sight to grow double from the single digits.

items.label: Honeywell Aerospace Jefferies Global Industrials Conference 2026 (09-09-2026)
items.signal_prefix: CEO Jim Currier on the commercial business: the commercial a

set.signal: CEO Jim Currier on the commercial business: the commercial aftermarket is 40% of the business, 60% commercial air transport and 40% business aviation, with the business-aviation segments 'growing significantly' running from super mid-size to ultra-long range, Honeywell Aerospace's sweet spot; retrofit mods and upgrades are about 10% of the business, growing double digit; many business-aviation contracts are power-by-the-hour, and he expects commercial aftermarket growth in excess of flight hours. In selectables Honeywell Aerospace historically won around 40% of the value competed and now 60% over the last 4,000 aircraft wins; IndiGo (800 aircraft) is the largest win, second a United Airlines win of 600 aircraft a couple of years ago. Margin expansion will come mostly from volume, then mix (more output to the aftermarket) and price as long-term agreements with multiple OEMs are renegotiated.

items.reason: The CEO said these business-aviation segments are 'growing significantly' (and are Honeywell Aerospace's sweet spot), not that demand is strongest there.
items.evidence: the certain segments of business aviation that are growing significantly are in that super mid-size category all the way up to ultra-long range, and that's the sweet spot
